ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: In order to study the structure and function of proteins, it is often necessary to separate and purify proteins from biological materials. A student used gel chromatography to separate and purify 3 kinds of proteins, A, B, and C, from a certain biological material, and performed SDS-polyacrylamide gel electrophoresis on the 3 purified proteins. The results are shown in the figure ("+" and "-" respectively represent the anode and cathode of the electrophoresis tank). It is known that the relative molecular mass of A is twice that of B, and both A and B are composed of one peptide chain. Answer the question: Gel chromatography can separate proteins according to differences in the relative molecular mass of proteins. Judging from the figure, among the 3 proteins A, B, and C, which protein is eluted first from the gel chromatography column?

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: In order to study the structure and function of proteins, it is often necessary to separate and purify proteins from biological materials. A student used gel chromatography to separate and purify 3 kinds of proteins, A, B, and C, from a certain biological material, and performed SDS-polyacrylamide gel electrophoresis on the 3 purified proteins. The results are shown in the figure ("+" and "-" respectively represent the anode and cathode of the electrophoresis tank). It is known that the relative molecular mass of A is twice that of B, and both A and B are composed of one peptide chain. Answer the question: Gel chromatography can separate proteins according to differences in the relative molecular mass of proteins. Judging from the figure, among the 3 proteins A, B, and C, which protein is eluted first from the gel chromatography column?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: The figure shows the results of SDS-polyacrylamide gel electrophoresis. The three lanes above are labeled A, B, and C in order; the right side shows the upper end as "-" and the lower end as "+". The A lane has only one band, located in the middle-upper part; the B lane has only one band, located lower than A; the C lane has two bands, of which the upper band is higher than the band of A, and the lower band is lower than near B. Then reason: In SDS-PAGE, proteins are denatured and are mainly separated according to the relative molecular mass of peptide chains. Proteins move toward the anode "+"; the smaller the molecular mass, the farther they migrate and the lower the band. A and B are both single peptide chains, and the relative molecular mass of A is twice that of B, which is consistent with the A band being higher than B in the figure. C shows two bands, indicating that C is composed of at least two peptide chains; the relative molecular mass of the upper peptide chain of C is greater than that of A, and adding the mass of the lower peptide chain indicates that the relative molecular mass of the complete C protein is the largest. In gel chromatography, the larger the relative molecular mass of the protein, the harder it is to enter the pores of the gel particles, and the shorter the path it passes through, so it is eluted first. Therefore, the one first eluted from the gel chromatography column is C.
